## Why Model Career Trajectories? {.smaller}

- Front offices are implicitly betting on the *shape of an aging curve* every time they sign a contract.
- Players face the same question from the inside: **which skills erode first**, and what should they train to compensate?
- Performance is **not one number**: a career is many curves at once
- What can we learn about aging in NBA athletes from multiple modalities of performance, and how can we use that to forecast careers?

::: notes
The Nets anecdote is the hook: misjudging two aging curves altered two franchises for a decade.
:::

## Prior Work {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip title="Production curve analysis"}
Infer smooth career trajectories $f_p(t)$ from **sparse, irregular longitudinal observations** across players — and use them to forecast, compare, and explain careers.
:::

**Bayesian modeling of Basketball Performance:**

- **Page, Fellingham & Reese (2007, JQAS)** — Bayesian hierarchical modeling of box-score contributions: which *positions'* skills actually contribute to winning.
- **Page, Barney & McGuire (2013, JQAS)** — production curves for NBA players: how position, usage rate, and minutes shape the aging arc — the closest ancestor of this work.

**Aging Curves and Player Pooling:**

- **Vaci et al. (2019)** — piecewise parametric aging curves, peak location fixed *a priori*
- **Wakim & Jin (2014)** — functional data analysis of aging curves 
- **Vinué & Epifanio (2019)** — players as convex combinations of fixed archetypoids
- **RAPTOR (FiveThirtyEight)** — single summary score via nearest-neighbor averaging of similar historical players

## Outline & Contributions {.smaller}

**Setup** — why career curves, prior work, the data, and mitigating selection-bias

::: {.fragment}
<span class="blueterm">Contribution 1</span> — **a nonlinear latent variable model for careers**: one learned player embedding (GPLVM → random Fourier features) drives 17 metric-appropriate likelihoods — plus a career-length (survival) likelihood that regularizes the embedding and corrects survivor bias
:::

::: {.fragment}
<span class="blueterm">Contribution 2</span> — **the Concave Process prior**: a nonparametric, full-support prior over concave functions with an analytic form and peak age / peak value as explicit parameters
:::

**Then** — results (trajectories, similarity, peak timing, calibration, draft cohorts), and future work on injury counterfactuals

## The Data {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
- ~**2,300 players**, seasons **1997–2026**, ages **18–38** (basketball-reference, via `ballr`)
- A $P \times T \times K$ tensor: players $\times$ ages $\times$ **17 metrics**
- Counts (BLK, STL, AST, REB, TOV), attempts (FGA, FTA), made-shot fractions (FG2%, FG3%, FT%), proportions (USG, minutes%), composites (OBPM, DBPM), games played
- Entries are **missing** when a player is injured, not yet in the league (left truncation),retired (right censoring), or outside the scope of the data collection (non-informative missingness)

:::

## The Selection-Bias Trap {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Cross-sectional averages at ages 35+ are computed **only over survivors** — disproportionately elite players.
- Several metric **averages** *turn upward* late in career.
- A flexible unconstrained model will happily fit it as a real feature.

[**Two coordinated fixes:**]{.fragment}

- A **concavity constraint** on the trajectory shape (this talk's centerpiece)
- A **survival model** for *who* is observed at all
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](../../model_output/model_plots/empirical_production.png)
:::

# Contribution 1: A Latent Variable Model For Careers {background-color="#003660"}

## Player Similarity Is Learned, Not Assumed {.smaller}

GPLVM-style latent embedding with a **structured prior**:

$$
X_p \sim \mathcal{N}\!\big(Z_p^\top W,\; \sigma_X^2 I_q\big), \qquad W \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_W^2 I)
$$

- $Z_p$ = (−log draft position, height, position dummies): a *scouting-informed anchor*
- $W$ is **learned jointly** — the data decide how much draft position and height actually predict latent location
- Rookies with 1 season of data are shrunk toward a sensible neighborhood; veterans are dominated by their own data
- Everything downstream reads $X_p$ through a **random Fourier feature** map $\phi$ (Rahimi & Recht 2007) — player similarity is a learned **exponential (SE) kernel**, with ARD relevances $\ell_j$ pruning unused dimensions — the **RFLVM** (Gundersen et al. 2021):

  $$
  \phi(X_p)^\top \phi(X_{p'}) \;\xrightarrow{m \to \infty}\; \exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{1}{2}\textstyle\sum_j \ell_j (X_{pj} - X_{p'j})^2\Big)
  $$

::: {.fragment}
```{r rff-demo}
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 2.4
#| fig-align: center
xg <- seq(-2, 2, by = 0.02)

ell_rel <- 2   # ARD relevance (inverse squared bandwidth), paper convention

kern_approx <- map_dfr(c(10, 50, 500), function(m) {
  om <- rnorm(m) * sqrt(ell_rel)
  tibble(m = paste0("m = ", m), x = xg,
         k = rowMeans(cos(outer(xg, om))))
}) |> mutate(m = factor(m, levels = paste0("m = ", c(10, 50, 500))))

exact <- tibble(x = xg, k = exp(-0.5 * ell_rel * xg^2))

lab_pos <- tibble(m = levels(kern_approx$m),
                  x = -1.95, k = c(0.95, 0.8, 0.65))

p_kern <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = kern_approx, aes(x, k, color = m), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = exact, aes(x, k), color = "black",
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = lab_pos, aes(x, k, label = m, color = m),
            hjust = 0, size = 3.4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1.08, label = "exact SE kernel",
           size = 3.4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(pal[c("orange", "aqua", "darkblue")])) +
  labs(title = "φ(x)'φ(0) → SE kernel (Bochner)",
       x = "x − x'", y = "k(x, x')") +
  theme_talk(base_size = 12)

p_kern
```
:::

# Contribution 2: The Concave Process Prior {background-color="#003660"}

## Concavity From A Squared GP {.smaller}

Force $h'' \le 0$: start from a line, subtract an accumulating, always-nonnegative curvature. **Every draw is concave.**

$$
h(t) \;=\; \beta_0 + \beta_1 (t - t_0) \;-\; \int_{t_0}^{t}\!\!\int_{t_0}^{s} \underbrace{[g(z)]^2}_{\ge\, 0} \, dz\, ds,
\qquad g \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, K)
$$

```{r construction-demo}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.1
#| fig-align: center
set.seed(1)
age_grid <- seq(18, 38, by = 0.1)
dz       <- 0.1
x        <- age_grid - mean(age_grid)
L        <- 2 * max(abs(x))
M        <- 10
ell      <- 1          # spectral bandwidth (as in sample_concave_prior)
sigma2   <- 0.25
peak_targets <- c(25, 28, 31)   # place each draw's peak at an interior age
n_draws  <- length(peak_targets)

ev  <- pi * (1:M) / (2 * L)
Sld <- sigma2 * exp(-0.5 * (ev / ell)^2)              # spectral density
Psi <- sqrt(1 / L) * sin(outer(x + L, ev))            # T x M basis matrix
phi <- make_convex_phi(x, L, M)                       # T x M x M (closed-form ∬ψψ)

draws <- map_dfr(1:n_draws, function(i) {
  a_til <- rnorm(M) * sqrt(Sld)
  g     <- as.vector(Psi %*% a_til)
  dbl   <- vapply(seq_along(x), function(t_idx) {
    as.numeric(t(a_til) %*% phi[t_idx, , ] %*% a_til)
  }, numeric(1))
  int_g2 <- c(0, diff(dbl)) / dz                      # ∫g² = d/dt of the double integral
  # slope β₁ = ∫g² at the target peak age  ⇒  f'(peak) = 0, peak lands in-range
  b_slope <- int_g2[which.min(abs(age_grid - peak_targets[i]))]
  f_raw <- b_slope * (x + L) - dbl
  # β₀ (free constant) chosen so each curve crests at 0 — makes the peak legible
  tibble(draw = factor(i), age = age_grid,
         g = g, g2 = g^2, f = f_raw - max(f_raw))
})

p1 <- ggplot(draws, aes(age, g, color = draw)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#9CBEBE") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(pal[c("darkblue", "aqua", "orange")])) +
  labs(title = "1.  g(t): a GP draw", x = "age", y = NULL) + theme_talk()

p2 <- ggplot(draws, aes(age, g2, color = draw)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#9CBEBE") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(pal[c("darkblue", "aqua", "orange")])) +
  labs(title = expression(bold("2.  g(t)"^2 >= 0 * ": forced curvature")),
       x = "age", y = NULL) + theme_talk()

p3 <- ggplot(draws, aes(age, f, color = draw)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(pal[c("darkblue", "aqua", "orange")])) +
  labs(title = expression(bold("3.  " * beta[1] * "(t+L) − ∬g" ^ 2 * ": concave")),
       x = "age", y = NULL) + theme_talk()

p1 + p2 + p3
```

::: {.callout-tip .fragment title="Proposition (full support)"}
The push-forward measure of $g \mapsto h$ puts **positive mass on every uniform neighborhood of every continuous concave function**
:::

## The Model At A Glance {.smaller}

For player $p$, age $t$, metric $k$:

$$
\mu_{ptk} = \underbrace{{\color{#09847A}{f^k(X_p, t)}}}_{\text{concave aging curve}} \;+\; \underbrace{{\color{#047C91}{r^k_p(t)}}}_{\mathrm{AR}(1)\ \text{deviation}}
\qquad
y_{ptk} \sim \mathcal{F}_k\!\left(g_k^{-1}(\mu_{ptk}),\, \phi_k,\, \omega_{ptk}\right)
$$

- ${\color{#003660}{X_p \in \mathbb{R}^q}}$: latent player embedding — **induces dependence across players *and* metrics** (Contribution 1)
- ${\color{#09847A}{f^k(X_p,t)}}$: concave in $t$ for every player and metric (Contribution 2)
- ${\color{#047C91}{r^k_p(t)}}$: idiosyncratic persistence (role changes, hot streaks) the aging curve shouldn't absorb
- $\mathcal{F}_k$: **metric-appropriate likelihood** with exposure $\omega_{ptk}$ (minutes, attempts, games)
- **Career exit is just one more likelihood**: a Gompertz survival model reading the same $X_p$ — it regularizes the latent space and corrects survivor bias 

## Respecting The Sampling Distribution {.smaller}

| Metric type | Examples | Likelihood | Link | Exposure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Made shots | FG2M, FG3M, FTM | (Beta-)Binomial | logit | attempts |
| Counts | BLK, STL, AST, REB, TOV | Poisson / Neg-Bin | log | minutes |
| Composites | OBPM, DBPM | Gaussian | identity | precision $\propto$ minutes |
| Proportions | USG, MIN% | Beta | logit | mean–variance map |
| Games played | GP | Beta-Binomial(82) | logit | — |
| Career length | exit age | Gompertz hazard | log | left-truncated, right-censored |

- No Gaussian approximation for low-minute players — a 10-minute-per-game rookie's FG3% carries exactly as much information as its 40 attempts justify.
- Career length enters the same way every metric does — one more head on the shared embedding, so *who is still playing* informs the latent space too.

```{r cohort-widget}
  var tbody = document.getElementById("cohort-tbody");

  var cohorts = rows.map(function(r) { return r.cohort; })

    .sort(function(a, b) { return b - a; });
  cohorts.forEach(function(c) {
    var ns = 2026 - c + 1;
    var o = document.createElement("option");
    o.value = c;
    o.textContent = c + " (" + ns + (ns === 1 ? " season" : " seasons") + ")";
    sel.appendChild(o);
  });
  function render() {
    var c = Number(sel.value);
    tbody.innerHTML = rows
      .filter(function(r) { return r.cohort === c; })
      .sort(function(a, b) { return a.rank - b.rank; })
      .map(function(r) {
        return "<tr><td>" + r.rank + "</td><td>" + r.name + "</td><td>" +
          (r.age == null ? "—" : r.age) + "</td><td>" + r.pos + "</td><td>" +
          fmt(r.peak_obpm, 1) + "</td><td>" + fmt(r.peak_age, 1) + "</td><td>" +
          r.p2 + "%</td><td>" + r.p3 + "%</td><td>" + r.p4 + "%</td><td>" +
          fmt(r.yrs_to_peak, 1) + "</td></tr>";
      }).join("");
  }
  sel.addEventListener("change", render);
  render();
})();
</script>
'))
```

::: notes
Yrs to Peak is the posterior mean OBPM peak age minus the last observed age (0.0 = already at peak); Peak Age is the actual posterior mean peak age. P(>x) integrates parameter and sampling uncertainty — probability of a breakout season at the projected peak.
:::

## Takeaways {.smaller}

1. <span class="blueterm">Contribution 1</span> — **one embedding, many likelihoods**: a structured GPLVM ties 17 metric-appropriate observation models to a single player representation — with career length as one more likelihood that regularizes the embedding and corrects survivor bias.
2. <span class="blueterm">Contribution 2</span> — **the Concave Process prior**: nonparametric, full support, an *analytic* HSGP form — reparameterized so peak age and peak value are first-class parameters.
3. **Payoffs**: posterior peaks, similarity retrieval with uncertainty, label-free archetypes, calibrated multi-season forecasts, draft-cohort projection.

## Future Work: Injury Counterfactuals {.smaller}

Latent-factor **injury offset** switched on at first major injury (Achilles, ACL, quad/patellar, spine) at onset $t^*_{pm}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu^k_{ptm} &= f^k(X_p, t) + \mathbb{1}\{t > t^*_{pm}\}\, \tau^k_{ptm} \\
\tau^k_{ptm} &\sim \mathcal{N}\!\big(w_m^\top \tau^*_k,\; \sigma^2_{mk}\big)
\end{aligned}
$$

- $f^k$ fit on pre-injury data → a **counterfactual career arc**; survival submodel picks up career-*length* effects
- Also ahead: richer injury dynamics (severity, recovery, decay), injury subtypes, understanding heterogeneity in recovery, and **causal inference** on the effect of injuries on career trajectories

![](../../model_output/nba_convex_max_tvlinearlvm_injury/holdout_last_k/mcmc/plots/causal/Kevin%20Durant_metrics_itt.png)

Durant post-Achilles: observed post-injury average (dashed blue) barely deviates from the aging counterfactual — consistent with a 7-footer whose game rests on shooting touch, not explosion. Caveats: no-unmeasured-confounding assumption; return-to-play selection (immortal-time bias).
:::

## Appendix: Sharing Strength — The Factor Model View {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

We assume 17 metrics for 2,300 players lie on a low-dimensional manifold. A classical factor model:

$$
y_p \;\approx\; \Lambda\, x_p + \varepsilon_p,
\qquad
y_p \in \mathbb{R}^{K},\;\; x_p \in \mathbb{R}^{q},\;\; q \ll K
$$

- A few latent **traits** $x_p$ drive all $K$ observed metrics through loadings $\Lambda$: $\operatorname{Cov}(y) = \Lambda \Lambda^\top + \Psi$ is low-rank plus noise.
- Basketball reading: a player's rebounding, blocks, and FG2A don't need 17 free parameters — they co-move because a few underlying traits (size, athleticism, skill, role) drive them all.
- In our model the "outcomes" being factorized are not raw stats but **curve parameters**: each metric's peak age, peak value, and curvature weights are readouts of $x_p$ — linear in this classical view, and generalized to nonlinear in the RFLVM.

## Appendix: Reparameterize By What You Care About {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

$\beta_0, \beta_1$ are not interpretable. But two constraints — $h({\color{#C43424}{t^*}}) = {\color{#C43424}{f^*}}$ and $h'({\color{#C43424}{t^*}}) = 0$ — pin them down exactly:

$$
h'(t) = \beta_1 - \int_{t_0}^{t} g(z)^2\, dz
\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
\beta_1 = \int_{t_0}^{{\color{#C43424}{t^*}}} g(z)^2\, dz
$$

Solving for $\beta_0$ and substituting back:

$$
h(t) \;=\; {\color{#C43424}{f^*}} \;+\; (t - {\color{#C43424}{t^*}})\!\int_{t_0}^{{\color{#C43424}{t^*}}} g(z)^2\, dz \;-\; \int_{t}^{{\color{#C43424}{t^*}}}\!\!\int_{t_0}^{s} g(z)^2\, dz\, ds
$$

- The prior is now parameterized directly by <span class="accent">peak value $f^*$</span> and <span class="accent">peak age $t^*$</span> — the two quantities every scout, GM, and agent argues about.
- We can put **informative priors on peaks** and read their **posteriors** off directly.
- Links are monotone, so $t^*$ and peak-value *rankings* survive the inverse link untouched — for every likelihood family.

::: notes
This reparameterization is why the model can answer "when does he peak" as a posterior, not a post-hoc curve summary. Note both integral terms vanish at t = t*, so the GP contributes zero variance at the peak.
:::

## Appendix: Making It Tractable — HSGP {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

The double integrals in the peak-parameterized prior above have no closed form for a generic GP — so approximate $g$ with the **Hilbert-space GP** basis (Solin & Särkkä 2020):

$$
g(t) \approx \sum_{l=1}^{J} S(\sqrt{\lambda_l})^{1/2}\, \alpha_l\, \psi_l(t),
\qquad \psi_l(t) = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{L}} \sin\!\big(\sqrt{\lambda_l}(t + L)\big),
\quad \alpha_l \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)
$$

Sinusoids integrate in closed form, so the peak-parameterized prior collapses to **quadratic forms** in $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$:

$$
f(t) = f^* + \boldsymbol{\alpha}^\top \Big[\, \Psi(t^*) - \Psi(t) + \Psi'(t^*)\,(t - t^*) \,\Big] \boldsymbol{\alpha},
\qquad
\Psi_{lz}(t) = \frac{\cos(\epsilon^{+}_{lz}(t{+}L)) - 1}{2L (\epsilon^{+}_{lz})^2} - \frac{\cos(\epsilon^{-}_{lz}(t{+}L)) - 1}{2L(\epsilon^{-}_{lz})^2}
$$

with $\epsilon^{\pm}_{lz} = \sqrt{\lambda_l} \pm \sqrt{\lambda_z}$ (diagonal replaces the second term with $(t+L)^2/4L$).

- **Cost:** $O(J^2)$ per evaluation, differentiable, GPU-friendly — MCMC-ready.
- Truncation converges **uniformly, almost surely** to the exact push-forward as $J \to \infty$.

## Appendix: The Full Generative Story {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

1. <span class="blueterm">Player heterogeneity</span> → latent embedding, anchored by scouting covariates:&nbsp; $X_p \sim \mathcal{N}(Z_p^\top W, \sigma_X^2 I_q)$
2. <span style="color:#09847A; font-weight:600">Concave aging curves</span> with peaks read from the embedding:&nbsp; $f^k(X_p, t) \sim \mathcal{MCP}(\Theta; X)$ — a multi-input GP $g(x,t) \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, K_x \otimes K_t)$, so one shared embedding drives all 17 curves
3. <span style="color:#047C91; font-weight:600">Short-term persistence</span>:&nbsp; $r^k_p(t) \sim \mathrm{AR}(1)$ per player-metric (+ a calendar-year era trend for pace/era effects)
4. <span class="accent">Career duration</span>:&nbsp; Gompertz hazard, parameters linked to the same feature map $\phi(X_p)$
5. **Metric-appropriate observation model**:&nbsp; $y_{ptk} \sim \mathcal{F}_k\big(g_k^{-1}(f^k(X_p,t) + r^k_p(t)),\, \phi_k,\, \omega_{ptk}\big)$

## Appendix: The Gompertz Hazard {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Gompertz proportional hazards** on exit age, left-truncated at entry, right-censored for active players:

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_p(a) &= \eta_p\, e^{\gamma_p a} \\[2pt]
\log \eta_p &= \eta_{\text{glob}} + \sigma_{\text{exit}}\, \phi(X_p)^\top \psi_{\text{exit}} \\[2pt]
\log \gamma_p &= \gamma_{\text{glob}} + \phi(X_p)^\top \psi_{\text{rate}}
\end{aligned}
$$

- Exponential-in-age hazard behaves in accordance with the law of senescence.
- Both parameters read the **same embedding** $\phi(X_p)$ as every other likelihood — career length regularizes the latent space.
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

```{r gompertz-demo}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-align: center
entry <- 19
eta0  <- 0.04
gammas <- c(0.10, 0.15, 0.25)
gcolors <- unname(pal[c("darkblue", "aqua", "orange")])

gomp <- map_dfr(gammas, function(g) {
  a <- seq(entry, 42, by = 0.1)
  H <- (eta0 / g) * (exp(g * (a - 18)) - exp(g * (entry - 18)))
  tibble(gamma = g, age = a,
         hazard = eta0 * exp(g * (a - 18)),
         surv = exp(-H))
}) |> mutate(glab = paste0("γ = ", gamma))

medians <- gomp |>
  group_by(glab) |>
  summarize(med = age[which.max(surv <= 0.5)], .groups = "drop")

labels_h <- gomp |> group_by(glab) |> slice_tail(n = 1)

ph <- ggplot(gomp, aes(age, hazard, color = glab)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = labels_h, aes(label = glab), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.6,
            size = 4, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = gcolors) +
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))) +
  labs(title = "hazard h(a)  (log scale)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_talk(base_size = 14)

ps <- ggplot(gomp, aes(age, surv, color = glab)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = medians |> left_join(gomp, by = "glab") |>
               filter(abs(age - med) < 0.05),
             aes(age, surv), size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, color = "#9CBEBE", linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_color_manual(values = gcolors) +
  labs(title = "P(still active at age a)  ·  dots = median exit age",
       x = "age", y = NULL) +
  theme_talk(base_size = 14)

ph / ps
```

:::

## Appendix: Inference {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

- **Sampling Difficulties:** factor-model rotational non-identifiability ⇒ multimodal posterior
- **MAP-initialized MCMC:** SGD MAP estimate → fix well-identified kernel hyperparameters (GP lengthscale/amplitude, structured-prior scales, global hazard offsets) → NUTS on everything else ($X_p$, curve weights, peaks, AR components).
- 4 chains × 2,000 post-warmup draws, thinned to 500 retained on a GPU
- **Procrustes alignment:** each draw's $X^{(s)}$ is rotated and aligned to the MAP frame,
  $\min_R \|\hat{X} - X^{(s)} R\|_F$ (SVD), before *any* latent-space summary — neighbor retrieval, clustering, uncertainty.
- Posterior predictive respects the exposure cascade: draw games → minutes | games → counts | minutes → percentages | counts. A zero-game draw zeroes the season downstream: production *and* career-length uncertainty in one draw.

## Appendix: The Concave Process In Code {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

The closed-form $\Psi(t)$, as implemented in the R sampler used for this deck's figures:

```{r show-code}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
make_convex_phi <- function(x, L, M = 5, eps = 1e-5) {
  eig_vals      <- (pi * (1:M)) / (2 * L)              # sqrt(lambda_l)
  sum_eig_vals  <- outer(eig_vals, eig_vals, "+")      # eps+
  diff_eig_vals <- outer(eig_vals, eig_vals, "-")      # eps-
  phi <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(length(x), M, M))
  for (idx in seq_along(x)) {
    cos_pos <- safe_cos_term(sum_eig_vals,  x[idx], L, eps)  # (1-cos(z))/(2L eps^2)
    cos_neg <- safe_cos_term(diff_eig_vals, x[idx], L, eps)  # ... l==z limit (x+L)^2/(4L)
    phi[idx, , ] <- cos_neg - cos_pos                        # Psi(x): M x M
  }
  phi
}

# curve for player p, metric k (quadratic form in the HSGP weights):
# mu(t) = c_max + a' [ Psi(t_max) - Psi(t) + Psi'(t_max) (t - t_max) ] a
```

- `safe_cos_term` blends in the analytic $l = z$ limit so the $\epsilon^-_{ll} = 0$ diagonal stays finite (and differentiable in the model).

## Appendix: MCMC Diagnostics {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

- $\hat{R} > 1.05$ fractions by metric: 15/17 metrics below 15% of player-age cells for $\mu_{ptk}$; AST is the hardest (40.8%) — genuinely player-specific, not a rotation artifact.
- Procrustes-aligned traces interleave across chains for individual players' $X_p$ coordinates.
- Latent dimension ablation: $q{=}10$ best mean holdout RMSE (0.924) and log-loss (3.99); $q{=}20$ wins zero metrics by log-loss.

## Appendix: What The Prior Knows About Uncertainty {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="46%"}
Conditioned on the peak, Isserlis' theorem gives

$$
\operatorname{Var}\big(f(t) \mid t^*, f^*\big) \approx \tfrac{3}{4}\,\sigma^4 \,(t - t^*)^4
$$

- **Zero GP variance at the peak** — all peak uncertainty comes from the prior on $f^*$ itself.
- Variance grows **quartically** with distance from the peak, scaling as $\sigma^4$.
- Mode location from $n$ ordered points converges at $n^{-2/5}$ (vs. $n^{-1/2}$ for a mean) — careers are $n \approx 5$–$12$ seasons. The prior puts precision **where the data can support it**.
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}

```{r variance-funnel}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-align: center
funnel_draws <- function(peak_age_var, peak_val_var, label) {
  sample_concave_prior(
    lengthscale = 1, variance = 0.10,
    peak_age = 27, peak_value = 1,
    peak_age_variance = peak_age_var, peak_value_variance = peak_val_var,
    n_samples = 400, num_basis = 10, age_grid = seq(18, 38, by = 0.25)
  ) |> mutate(panel = label)
}

funnel <- bind_rows(
  funnel_draws(1e-12, 1e-12, "peak (t*, f*) known exactly"),
  funnel_draws(1.5^2, 0.4^2, "peak uncertain: t* ~ N(27, 1.5²), f* ~ N(1, 0.4²)")
)

band <- funnel |>
  group_by(panel, age) |>
  summarize(lo = quantile(value, 0.025), hi = quantile(value, 0.975),
            .groups = "drop")

spaghetti <- funnel |> filter(sample_id <= 25)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(age, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              fill = pal["lightblue"], alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_line(data = spaghetti, aes(age, value, group = sample_id),
            color = pal["blue"], alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 27, color = pal["orange"],
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "age", y = "f(t)",
       subtitle = "95% prior band (400 draws), 25 shown") +
  theme_talk(base_size = 14)
```

## Appendix: From One Curve To A Population {.smaller visibility="uncounted"}

Extend $g$ to a **multi-input GP** $g(x, t) \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, K_x \otimes K_t)$ and let the integration constants depend on $x$:

$$
f(x,t) = f^*(x) + \phi(x)^\top \mathbf{A}^\top \Big[ \Psi(t^*(x)) - \Psi(t) + \Psi'(t^*(x))(t - t^*(x)) \Big] \mathbf{A}\, \phi(x)
$$

- $\phi(x)$: feature map with $\phi(x)^\top \phi(x') \approx K_x(x, x')$ — linear $\phi(x) = x$, or random Fourier features ($m{=}50$, ARD lengthscales)
- Peak age $t^*(x)$ and peak value $f^*(x)$ are read from the **same feature map** — similar players share peaks, ceilings, *and* curve shapes
- Plug in $x = X_p$: one shared 10-d embedding drives **all 17 metrics** + survival
